Minutes:

- **Meeting Time Adjustment** Chris Wilson proposed modifying the meeting schedule based on poll results, suggesting keeping the APAC-EMEA meeting (1:00 a.m. Pacific time) and converting the Americas-APAC meeting (4:00 p.m. Pacific) to another Americas-EMEA time slot (9am Pacific).  We remain open to feedback, especially from APAC attendees, if the remaining time is insufficient.
- **TPAC Agenda and Scheduling** Chris Wilson noted that agenda suggestions for TPAC are being collected in issue [11711](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11711) and they will start compiling the agenda next week. They also confirmed that the regular meetings immediately preceding TPAC (November 6th) and during TPAC week (November 13th) will be canceled due to travel and the conference.
- **XSLT Removal Stage Advancement** Mason Freed reported that XSLT removal had already been agreed to move to stage two a couple of weeks prior and sought approval to advance it to stage three, citing existing specification text and two implementer supports as the entry criteria. Anne van Kesteren agreed to the stage three advancement, suggesting that the text should be merged once it is stable in implementations, such as after a month in stable Chrome, following the precedent set by mutation events and risky changes guidelines. Mason Freed noted that the deprecation process is planned to be year-long. Brian Kardell suggested people might interpret moving forward in the process here as "google doesn't care", and offered to Google folks to come on Igalia chats and talk about it if they want.
- **Form Control Range Stage Advancement** Stephanie Zhang proposed moving "form control range" to stage two, explaining it as a live abstract range subclass intended to support range-style geometry and selection APIs for native form controls . Anne van Kesteren mentioned that Ryosuke had previously suggested an alternative API shape (extending the `Range` class instead of using `AbstractRange`), which Stephanie Zhang explained was avoided due to complications with maintaining encapsulation and inherited behaviors . Anne van Kesteren agreed to review the suggestion by the following week.
- **Customized Built-in Elements via Element Internals** Alex Keng presented an update on the proposal to enable custom elements with button activation behavior, specifically `command` and `command for`, stating there is consensus on supporting these attributes, reflected properties (though location is not final), and a `command event`. Olli Pettay and Anne van Kesteren sought clarification on whether reflected properties would be exposed to the outside world or only within `ElementInternals`, with Alex Keng confirming the latter, requiring authors to implement getters and setters on the custom element.
   - **Bundling of Features and Focusability Concerns** The discussion shifted to the bundling of features under an opt-in mechanism and future incremental additions, with Mason Freed expressing concern if all future behaviors were added under a single static flag. Alex Keng confirmed they plan to move away from a single static property and use another mechanism for future features like `button type`. Lea Verou suggested that perhaps instead of adding another static later we can allow overloading the current static with an object that parameterizes _which_ button activation behaviors we are including.  Luke raised concerns that implementing `command` and `command for` should implicitly include focusability and an implicit ARIA role of `button` for accessibility, which is a prerequisite for most button behaviors.
   - **Focusability and Use Case Debate** Simon Pieters and Keith Cirkel debated the implications of default focusability, noting that not all form-associated elements are focusable by default and that complex widgets might require different focus handling. Lea Verou suggested that the feature design should consider future support for ECMAScript mixins. Luke and Keith Cirkel emphasized the need to fully understand developer use cases, noting that requests like `href` and leading/trailing icons may not be fully addressed by just implementing `command` and `command for`. Taylore Givens confirmed that customers like Reddit and Fluent Design System want focusability and that the command/command for support was specifically requested by Fluent Design System.  Noam Rosenthal suggested it would be good to see somewhere a summary of "this is the kind of thing people are trying to do but can't because ElementInternals etc. is lacking" for when we talk about APIs/solutions.
- **Focus Without User Activation Proposal** Update Fernando Fiori provided an update on the pull request for focus without user activation, stating that they have been gathering more information from partners and customers. Taylore Givens summarized the core issue is whether a parent frame should be allowed to set focus when the focus is currently on a cross-origin child iframe, arguing this should be allowed because parent frames already have indirect ways to regain focus and it aligns with existing platform behavior.

Action items:

1. Chris Wilson will start putting the agenda together next week for TPAC.
2. Anne van Kesteren will take the question about the API shape for form control range back to Ryosuke and try to respond by next week.
3. The group will carry over the proposal for customized built-in element via element internals to next week for further discussion.
4. Chris Wilson will edit the meeting series to drop the Americas and APAC meeting and change it to the EMEA and America time slot.
5. Chris Wilson will talk to the other hosts about making sure to turn on the automated stuff for all the meetings and get into a regular cycle to do it a little more consistently.
